question: Which exact 3.1.190 entry points back the Supervisor platform services already recovered on Band 9 3.1.32 (monotonic clock, heap, lseek/mkdir/rmdir/fsync, battery, wake locks, screen state and wake, manual brightness, properties, MiWear link state, LVGL service timer), and which earlier ensemble records are wrong?
prototype_hypothesis: Same AAPCS contracts as the Band 9 3.1.32 platform hooks (EVID-PLATFORM-HW-9132-001), called from the UI owner thread.
callsite_evidence: NuttX functions carry their source path in DEBUGASSERT (strings referenced through the 0x2C000000 alias): clock/clock_gettime.c -> 0xC0BB094, vfs/fs_lseek.c -> lseek 0xC37E1F4 (fs_getfilep 0xC37C0D0, file_seek 0xC37A50C), vfs/fs_mkdir.c -> 0xC37E248, vfs/fs_rmdir.c -> 0xC37F774, vfs/fs_fsync.c -> 0xC37FE20, mm_heap/mm_malloc.c -> mm_malloc 0xC0F0BB0 behind malloc 0xC0F1170, mm_heap/mm_free.c -> mm_free 0xC0F066C behind free 0xC0F0790 (both on the user heap 0x200B0D44; kmm_malloc 0xC0F11F4 / kmm_free 0xC0F07A4 use the kernel heap 0x200B0840).
clock_gettime writes {int64 tv_sec, int32 tv_nsec}; MiWearScreen 0xC44E2D8 zeroes a 16-byte buffer, calls it with CLOCK_REALTIME and computes tv_sec*1000000 + tv_nsec/1000.
lseek stores the 64-bit offset from r2:r3, loads whence from the first stack argument and returns -1 in r0:r1 on error, the same shape as 3.1.32.
mkdir passes mode (r1) & ~umask to the mountpoint mkdir (ops +0x50); without a mountpoint it reserves a pseudo directory.
struct stat is 96 bytes here as on 3.1.32 (stat pseudo helper 0xC37FA64 clears 96 bytes, st_size at +24), not the 104-byte layout the Supervisor expects, so stat is not recorded.

uv_topic_battery_state_cb 0xC44AB28 (PowerManager, also logs set_battery_state_from_topic_data) sets the charging-ready byte 0x200BD308 and the level-ready byte 0x200BD309, the charging flag 0x200BD30C and the level dword 0x200BD310; 0xC4487CC returns ready-and-ready.

PowerManager wakelock_create 0xC44CE60 accepts levels 6 and 26, logs 'succeeded, levelAndFlags=%lu, tag=%s', stores the tag at +8 and wraps a 'wakelock' screen session at +32; acquire 0xC44E890 counts at +20 and on the first hold calls screen_session_start(s, 1) and, with flag 0x10000000, screen_turn_on("wakelock", 26); release 0xC44E970 stops the session on the last release.

MiWearScreen logs __func__ for every session call: screen_session_create 0xC44BC10, start 0xC44C9FC (tag, handle, auto_stop), stop 0xC44CA88, set_auto_brightness 0xC44CD04 (status names UNSPECIFIED/ENABLED/DISABLED at 0x2C751980, so 2 = DISABLED), set_brightness_value 0xC44CD94, restore_default 0xC44CC0C, screen_turn_on 0xC44E76C. The stock NFC near_reminder caller 0xC34A43C runs create -> set_brightness_value(s, 128) -> set_auto_brightness(s, 2) -> start(s, 0), the order the Supervisor uses.

screen_get_state 0xC448910 returns 2 while a keep-on hold is counted (0x200B5D8C), otherwise the applied state byte 0x200B5D94; async_apply_screen_state_change 0xC44E340 names states OFF/AOD/ON (0/1/2).

The settings writers 0xC44CCA0 / 0xC44CCCC persist persist.screen.auto_brightness and persist.screen.brightness_value (clamped 31..255); MiWearScreen init 0xC374200 reads them through property_get_int32 0xC49D95C.

property_get 0xC49D7C0 queries kvdbd over a socket, returns the value length (up to 255 bytes plus NUL) or -22 for a missing key with a NULL default; property_get_int32 0xC49D95C is property_get(key, buf, NULL) + strtol(buf, &end, 0) returning the default on error or trailing characters.

system_get_state 0xC36A340 clears out[0..1], reads system_all_state through the pointer 0x200BA444 and spins with 'Please call system_init_state first.' while it is NULL; state 1 is byte +1 (get_connect_state).

lv_timer_create 0xC25A288 inserts into the timer list 0x200BF30C that lv_timer_handler 0xC25A0E8 (./lvgl/src/misc/lv_timer.c) walks, stores period +0, last_run +4, callback +8, user_data +12, repeat_count -1; lv_indev_drv_register 0xC25A2D4 calls it as (read_timer_cb, 16, indev). lv_timer_del 0xC258698 removes from the same list, sets timer_deleted and frees through lv_mem_free 0xC258498 -> free 0xC0F0790; lv_timer_handler calls it when a timer's repeat_count reaches 0.

Ensemble records refuted: clock_gettime 0xC36EA34 is a connection-slot registration helper (returns -95/-12/-98/-105), heap_malloc 0xC41A3D8 a C++ copy helper, heap_free 0xC41DD18 a C++ virtual-call thunk, lseek 0xC2A61C0 the media app's media_refresh_page_cb, lv_timer_create 0xC4B47C8 and lv_timer_del 0xC4B47B0 thunks, bt_adapter_get_instance 0xC27AD30 a wrapper that builds the Alipay enter_bind_tip page, bt_adapter_get_state 0xC454E34 a message handler reading system_all_state 2. The Supervisor generated before this review called 0xC36EA35 as its monotonic clock.
ownership_analysis: Wake-lock objects and brightness sessions are created once per Supervisor slot and kept; wakelock_create and screen_session_create store the tag pointer, so the tag must be static. heap_malloc/heap_free share the user heap. Nothing here takes ownership of caller buffers beyond the call.
unsafe_assumptions: Battery level/charging have no callable getter on this build: callers read 0x200BD30C/0x200BD310 directly and 0xC4A9F08 copies the pair into the fixed global 0x200CDCF0 instead of an out-parameter, so the battery service reads the pair itself: power_battery_state 0x200BD30C (charging byte +0, level word +4) behind power_battery_ready (added 2026-11-03).

The vibrator is preset-only: miwear_vibrator_run 0xC45DC68 takes a 12-byte block whose type byte selects one of 23 stock patterns (1..23), with no waveform kind byte or duration; miwear_vibrator_cancel 0xC45DD24 cancels by id. No vibrator_run/vibrator_cancel is recorded, so haptics stays UNSUPPORTED.
No Bluetooth adapter getter/state entry point was recovered (no framework adapter API strings); both ensemble records are withdrawn and adapter state stays unknown.
stat is not recorded (96-byte struct stat); the Supervisor's opendir + lseek fallback is used.
recommended_probe: all-services-test on Mirage (emulator evidence only), then on a device: wake lock, wake screen, brightness override, property reads and MiWear link state.
